plan.title: Task View Filtering & Search
plan.overview: Implement a QuickPick-based "Find Task" command accessible from the KANBAN TASKS header. The command populates a QuickPick with all tasks showing ID, title, labels, status, and priority. When user selects a task, it reveals that task in the TreeView by expanding its parent column and selecting it. This follows VSCode's native navigation pattern (Cmd+P, Cmd+Shift+O) since TreeView API does not support inline filtering.

approach.rationale: VSCode TreeView API does not support inline filter/search (GitHub issue #50062 open since 2018). QuickPick is the standard VSCode pattern for search/navigation. This approach: - Uses native VSCode QuickPick with matchOnDescription and matchOnDetail for fuzzy search - Leverages existing loadAllTasks() function to populate QuickPick items - Uses TreeView.reveal() API to expand column and highlight selected task - Follows existing header action pattern for button placement (see package.json:103-118) - Follows existing command registration pattern (see extension.ts:232-238)

task.action: - Open VSCode with a workspace containing .kanban/tasks/ folder - Verify search icon appears in KANBAN TASKS header (FR1) - Click the search icon - Verify QuickPick appears with all tasks (FR2) - Verify each item shows "ID: Title" format (FR3) - Verify labels shown as "#label1 #label2" (FR4) - Verify detail shows "Status: ... | Priority: ..." (FR5) - Type partial task ID or title, verify fuzzy matching works (FR6) - Select a task - Verify the task's parent column expands (FR8) - Verify the task is highlighted/selected in TreeView (FR7) - Clear filter by pressing Escape, verify all tasks visible again

testing.automated: None required - this is UI functionality that relies on VSCode APIs. Unit testing QuickPick and TreeView.reveal() would require mocking VSCode internals which provides limited value.
testing.manual: - Click search icon in KANBAN TASKS header - Verify QuickPick shows all tasks with proper formatting - Type partial ID (e.g., "00") and verify matching tasks shown - Type partial title and verify matching tasks shown - Select a task and verify it's revealed in TreeView - Verify parent column expands when task is selected - Press Escape to cancel and verify tree unchanged
testing.regression: - Verify existing header buttons (Discovery, Create, Refresh) still work - Verify TreeView still displays correctly after using find - Verify file watcher refresh still works

reveal() handles this gracefully per VSCode API
